headline: Large Energy Users Pay Grid Costs
short_summary: This bill requires large energy users, primarily data centers, to pay for the increased electric generating capacity and infrastructure costs they create, rather than shifting these costs to residential ratepayers.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP1123) on 2026-05-14
supporters: Residential ratepayers, consumer advocacy groups, Governor Spanberger, environmental groups.
opponents: Data center industry, large industrial energy users.
news_headline: Governor Spanberger Signs Legislation to Address High Energy Costs & Rejoin RGGI
news_summary: Governor Abigail Spanberger signed legislation aimed at addressing high energy costs for Virginians and ensuring data centers do not drive up costs for families. The new laws protect ratepayers from shouldering the cost of new energy infrastructure investments by data centers and other high-load energy customers.

headline: Data Centers Report Water Usage
short_summary: This bill mandates water utilities to report the total volume of water provided to data centers, increasing transparency on their water consumption.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Environmental groups, local communities, water conservationists, Virginia League of Conservation Voters, Senator Kannan Srinivasan.
news_headline: New Virginia law requires data center water usage be made public
news_summary: A new Virginia law mandates local water authorities to report data center water usage, making the numbers publicly available on the Department of Environmental Quality's website. This legislation aims to provide transparency regarding the significant water consumption of data centers, which has been a growing concern for communities.

headline: Data Center Siting and Noise Rules
short_summary: This bill establishes a permit process for high energy use facilities, requiring site assessments for noise and other impacts on nearby communities before approval.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Local communities, residents near proposed data center sites, environmental groups.
news_headline: A Roanoke Delegate Helped Write Virginia's New Data Center Law. Here's What It Does, and What It Doesn't
news_summary: Virginia's new law, HB 153, which took effect July 1, 2026, requires developers of large data centers to conduct site assessments examining noise profiles on nearby homes and schools. While it mandates studies and disclosures, the law does not set specific noise limits, water caps, or setbacks, leaving some discretion to localities.
